name: persoonsnummer
note: Aruba's sheet (its government's own sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Tax Identification Numbers'; the OECD's index page sits behind a bot check and wasn't opened, the sheet itself came straight back)), read 2026-10-30: the TIN, in Dutch the persoonsnummer, is allocated to a person who asks the Tax Department for it, the same for every tax; eight digits generated by the system. No check digit, fee or time is stated. Aruba keeps its own number, apart from the Netherlands'.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Aruba: Information on Tax Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: A TIN (in Dutch called “persoonsnummer”) is allocated to a natural person or entity if the person or entity ... requests this at the Tax Department. ... The TIN is generated by the automated system after registering certain data of a tax payer and exists of 8
